[b]June 13, 2028: The National Assembly[/b]

The King of Montfleur, having been made aware of the growing matter in their southern neighbour, Rosenmarkke, would seek to bring the matter to the National Assembly, convening an extraordinary session of the assembly and the senate, and he made his case for the matter.

My friends and fellow strivers of this our government,

Regarding the disturbances that have begun to occur to the south of our nation, it is not right for Montfleur to get involved.

Jeers from the nationalists roared from one side of the chamber as the king paused. 

However, continued the king, Should the people of Rosenmarkke call upon our aide, I ask you, is it not right to help them?

He paused again as jeers filled the hall from the left coalition this time.

My friends, neutrality has done Montfleur a bad way, it has left her far behind her peers, and has shown to be ineffective in the preservation of this state, I ask you, should our friends and allies in Rosenmarkke call for our help, will we not help them?

More jeers from the left, the king leaned on his right and pointed at them from the podium.

The era of Les Optimistes, it is over, for too long the ideals of peace and harmony have threatened our very state, should the topic of merging with Rosenmarkke come forward, I say we vote yes! Yes! Yes! declared Henri, pounding the podium. 

The assembly hall filled with the roar of yess and nos and jeers as the deputies of the chamber forced their way into the throng of legislators who had left their seats and now filled the aisles of the chamber, shouting slogans for or against the motion. 

I say we vote yes! And more than this, I say we begin to move towards facilitating the union! Through the formation of a congress of constitution! declared Henri, shouting over the roar. 

At this point, Eleonore had begun to bang the gavel on the podium to demand order; however, the king's words had incensed the legislators greatly as those in the communist party ripped off their wigs and stomped on them, while the moderates were jostled about by their peers, and the nationalist factions were cheering and shouting. 

My dear friends, continued the king over the roar, The process will be long, and it will be hard, but we must consider the possibilities that may come in the following months, should the discontent in Rosenmarkke among its citizens rise to the point where the government is unable to sustain itself, and the regions and estates of Rosenmarkke begin passing resolutions to secede from Rosenmarkke to join Montfleur, which is a possibility, we must be ready,

The roar continued as guards moved to the sides of the podium, attempting to usher the king out. We will win! Montfleur always wins! declared Henri, lifting his cane and waving it as the guards pushed him out the back door of the chamber.
